main_text.p: jus seculi turbis separet. Cernimus quam studiose quivis suæ sectæ traditiones colat, quanto labore quam follicitè in vanū viam salutis, vitæ asperitate, sine fide salutari captet: solus qui purā Christi doctrinā gaudet, quia apertam sibi videt cælorum ianuam, neglecto introitu, Dei bonitatem contemnit. En stupendam stultitiā hominum; quia Dei verus cultus in justitiā, pace, & gaudio Spiritus Sancti, arctissimāq; animi per fidem cum Deo conjunctione consistit, ideò negligitur ut facillimus, jamq; peractus putatur, antequam leviculum ejus experimentum habeatur. Si contra durus foret ac horridus, si cum Indorū sacerdotibus oculi effodiendi essent, cum Turcarū superstitiosis ferro cutis dissecanda, cum Monachis nudis pedibus ambulandum, & lacera veste mendicandū, tum mirum in his studium ferveret, ut aliquid sibi mereri suo invento, mundoque admirabiles & Sancti videri possent. Fastidiosum vero est, nudis Christi meritis ut fruantur, solumque debitum præstare videantur, aliquid tædij suscipere: at in hoc tantummodo vera salus est, in hoc maxima difficultas: quia corporis labor in his requisitus, hominum infirmissimo quidem facilis est, ars vero & prudentia, animi-mique

page.notes: Printed text is in a classical 17th-century roman with long s; long s rendered as s. "suo invento" and "ut aliquid sibi mereri" are read from a slightly blurred line and may need checking. "seculi" is read from a faint ligature ([?] not applied as the letter is clear enough). The hyphenated word "ani-" continues to the catchword "mique" at the foot; the catchword is written as printed, and the joined word is rendered as "animi-mique" in the paragraph, which should be checked against the printed form: the page shows "ani-" at the line end and "mique" below, so the word is "animique".
